Overarching Evidence Recommendation: The population should be a defined patient group that reflect the intended population in the relevant healthcare setting
Explanatory notes: Define the target population including clinical parameters, subgroups, eligibility and contraindications. Patient groups should be in line with the DHT’s intended purpose and regulatory approval. Eligibility criteria for using the DHT and inclusion in the study should be reported.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide detailed information of baseline patient characteristics and demographics
Explanatory notes: Relevant patient information may include age, gender, ethnicity, sex, socioeconomic status, disability or cognitive impairment, education level, diagnosis and symptom severity, medicines and comorbidities. Describe also other important covariates chosen with input from clinical specialists.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: People in the comparison (control) group should be similar to those in the intervention (DHT) group
Explanatory notes: Both groups should have similar patient populations (including demographics and digital literacy levels) from similar healthcare services.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Studies should reflect the clinical setting where the DHT is intended to be used
Explanatory notes: Settings in the evidence should reflect standard care in the relevant healthcare service. Provide detailed descriptions of the services and settings in which the study is done, including referral and care pathways. This is especially important if people can access the intervention through different referral pathways (e.g. self-referral, healthcare professional referral etc.). Ideally, studies should be run across multiple centres that represent the variety of the referral and care pathways in the healthcare service.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Studies should reflect the clinical setting where the DHT is intended to be used
Explanatory notes: Studies should be conducted in Germany to ensure that results are applicable and meaningful to the care context. In some cases, studies outside of Germany may be considered if evidence is provided showing sufficient comparability of care.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: The intervention should be on the DHT in question and any associated accessories
Explanatory notes: The evidence should clearly state which technology was used, specifically the technology name, version, configuration settings, and any specific modules or features used.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: The intervention should be on the DHT in question and any associated accessories
Explanatory notes: If the DHT has been updated using a different or larger dataset or any other model updates (such as changing decision thresholds), then new evidence is needed on the updated version of the technology.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Delivery of the intervention in clinical studies should reflect how it is intended to be used in real-world clinical settings
Explanatory notes: This includes the conditions of the clinical setting and the level of healthcare professional support provided. DHTs intended to be used as unguided interventions (i.e. without healthcare professional support) must have evidence showing this intended use. Evidence on guided use of the technology is not directly transferable.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: DHTs in clinical studies should be used for a duration that reflects standard clinical practice
Explanatory notes:
Data should be collected in both the intervention and comparator groups from the point at which people would typically be offered the technology.
Long-term data should be collected to evaluate the effectiveness of the technology during and after use.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Studies should have sufficiently long follow-up to capture benefits and risks from using the technology
Explanatory notes:
Evidence on the use and effects of the DHT should be provided for a sufficiently long period of time to capture associated benefits, risks, costs and resource use, and system effects.
Ideally, evidence should be provided for a minimum of 6 months with longer follow-up (e.g. 12 to 18 months) where appropriate. The length of the follow-up period should be informed by relevant clinical and patient experts and guidelines.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: The comparators should reflect current practice or standard of care
Explanatory notes:
The choice of comparator (i.e. the control) should reflect standard care in the relevant healthcare setting and should be informed by clinical experts and guidelines. Standard care may differ across countries.
Relevant comparators may include:
• standard treatment (treatment as usual) without the use of the DHT
• no treatment or waiting list
• treatment with another DHT that is currently used in the care pathway
• non-digital delivery of the same intervention (e.g. paper-based version)

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: The comparators should reflect current practice or standard of care
Explanatory notes: If there is currently no standard care treatment for the target condition, a sham or active control may be the most appropriate choice of comparator to control for digital placebo effects.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Outcomes should include individual and system-level indicators that are relevant to assessing the use of the DHT in real life
Explanatory notes:
Relevant outcomes include clinical outcomes, patient-reported outcomes, usability and acceptability, and engagement measures such as adherence and satisfaction.
Select appropriate outcomes for the DHT's intended purpose, technology purpose, target population, and claimed benefits.
Consider which outcomes are most relevant to demonstrate the claimed benefits and risks of using the DHT in the specified healthcare setting.
Outcomes may be collected from patients, healthcare professionals, parents or carers. Where children are the intended user of the DHT, evidence should include children's responses of their own health state.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Outcomes should include individual and system-level indicators that are relevant to assessing the use of the DHT in real life
Explanatory notes: Outcomes should demonstrate the added clinical and organisational value from using the DHT. The main assessment criteria for clinical added value include mortality, morbidity and quality of life.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Outcomes should include individual and system-level indicators that are relevant to assessing the use of the DHT in real life
Explanatory notes:
Outcomes should focus on patient-centred effects including medical benefits and patient-relevant improvements of structure and processes. Wider organisational, productivity or economic outcomes cannot be used as primary endpoints for patient-centred effects.
Patient-relevant endpoints for medical benefits include morbidity, mortality and quality of life.
Patient-relevant improvements of structure and processes may include:
• coordinating treatment
• aligning treatment with guidelines or standards
• adherence
• increasing access to care
• safety
• health literacy
• patient autonomy
• coping with illness in daily living
• reducing treatment-related difficulties for patients and carers.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Outcomes should be recorded at baseline and at appropriate timepoints throughout the study or evidence generation period
Explanatory notes:
Outcomes should be recorded before the intervention has been offered, at appropriate intervals throughout the intervention, at the end of the intervention, and at follow-up (e.g. 6 to 18 months after the intervention). The timings of these intervals will depend on the specific intervention and target condition but should be frequent and long enough to capture the short and long-term benefits and risks of using the technology.
Clearly report any missing longitudinal data, attrition and steps taken to reduce loss to follow-up.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Outcomes must include test accuracy and time to diagnosis. Evidence should also be provided showing the effects of using the DHT on clinical decision making, healthcare outcomes, and system effects
Explanatory notes:
Relevant performance outcomes include:
• test accuracy in the intended healthcare setting, including accuracy when used by different types of healthcare professionals. This should include overall accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, c-statistic, and the number of true positives, false positives, true negatives and false negatives.
• cases of diagnostic disagreement between the DHT and current clinical practice and the likely reason for disagreement
• diagnostic accuracy of the DHT in different populations
• failure rate or rate of inconclusive reports, including reasons for failure
• number of missed diagnoses
• rate of further injury related to missed diagnoses
• proportion of people who need further testing
• additional reviews by specialists

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clinical outcomes should include intermediate and longer-term outcomes demonstrating symptom change, health-related quality of life, adverse events, and health service use
Explanatory notes:
Examples of relevant clinical outcomes include:
• remission, relapse and mortality
• health-related quality of life
• behaviour change
• medication use and adherence
• adverse events from using the DHT
• time to definitive treatment
• number of healthcare appointments, e.g. GP visits, specialist consultations, admissions etc.
• length of hospital stay
• hospital readmissions
• reduction of more intensive care
• number of days missed from school or work
• uptake of follow-on treatment after using the DHT
• longevity of any clinical benefits, such as longer term remission, relapse and mortality

Clinical studies should include condition-specific standardised measures and reflect outcomes recorded in real-world clinical practice.
Where possible and appropriate, condition-specific measures should be mapped to a standardised preference-based measure of health related quality of life (HRQoL) such as the EuroQol 5-Dimension questionnaire (EQ-5D). If mapping is used, the method and associated uncertainty should be reported.
Ensure that health-related quality of life outcomes are relevant to the population and intervention, and usable in economic modelling.
If studies use a surrogate outcome (i.e. an indirect measure intended to predict a clinically meaningful outcome) its validity and relevance must be demonstrated with literature or reference to guidelines.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clinical outcomes should include intermediate and longer-term outcomes demonstrating symptom change, health-related quality of life, adverse events, and health service use
Explanatory notes:
Additional treatment outcomes may include:
• impact on daily life such as self-esteem, school and work attendance, social functioning
• patient-reported outcomes such as pain, physical functioning, self-efficacy, psychological outcomes
• changes in symptom severity using recognised clinical measures
• rates of conversion to more intense or invasive treatments
• survival and need for revision procedures
• procedure-related discomfort

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clinical outcomes should include intermediate and longer-term outcomes demonstrating symptom change, health-related quality of life, adverse events, and health service use
Explanatory notes:
In addition to performance outcomes, evidence should also be provided showing the impact of using the DHT on clinical decision making, delivery of care, and clinical outcomes. Relevant clinical outcomes may include:
• number of referrals for treatment following diagnosis or detection using the technology, including number of unnecessary referrals
• adverse events
• clinical outcomes associated with missed diagnoses, misdiagnosis or inaccurate results
• time to diagnosis or discharge
• time to further referral or treatment
• number of further assessment appointments and attendance rates
• pre- and post-diagnosis treatment status
• changes in patient outcomes associated with use of the DHT
• clinically significant changes in treatment decisions when using the DHT
• changes in treatment and service use

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clinical outcomes should include intermediate and longer-term outcomes demonstrating symptom change, health-related quality of life, adverse events, and health service use
Explanatory notes: Provide evidence of the rate of diagnostic disagreement with healthcare professional review over time to show the potential for automation bias after deployment.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Outcomes on engagement and acceptability should be collected from patients and healthcare professionals
Explanatory notes:
Relevant outcomes may be collected via semi-structured interview or survey, and may include:
• acceptance
• satisfaction
• acceptability and user preferences
• access and intervention uptake
• usage data stratified by demographic variables
• ease of use and benefits of additional features
• healthcare professional-reported reasons for not offering the intervention to certain people
• reasons for not using the technologies
• perceived quality of the intervention or DHT

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Outcomes on engagement and acceptability should be collected from patients and healthcare professionals
Explanatory notes:
Relevant outcomes may include:
• adherence
• completion and attrition rates including reason for stopping treatment and characteristics of people who stop treatment prematurely
• engagement metrics (e.g. time spent per session or number of logins) and session completion rate
• patient-reported barriers to accessing or using the DHT
• feedback from excluded people or people who declined to take part

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of the economic and resource impact of using the DHT in the specified healthcare setting compared with standard care
Explanatory notes:
Provide short and long-term costs of implementing, integrating, maintaining and using the DHT over at least 12 months. Economic and resource impact outcomes may include but are not limited to:
• licence and maintenance fees with subscription duration
• costing structures to procure and implement the DHT (e.g. upfront, leasing, free-loan)
• technology acquisition and payment model used
• training costs to support the service
•costs to integrate the DHT with existing digital healthcare systems
• other technology costs (including additional hardware or software, cybersecurity)
• ongoing costs such as system updates, governance and technical support
• estimates of the number of people eligible to use the technology based on incidence and prevalence data
• number and cost of appointments in primary, secondary and community care
• additional interactions with healthcare professionals outside of appointments
• long-term follow-up costs needed to maintain effectiveness
• medication use
• changes in resource use associated with implementing and using the technology such as healthcare professional staff time and time saved
• impact of long-term effectiveness on long-term costs
• budget impact analysis

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of the economic and resource impact of using the DHT in the specified healthcare setting compared with standard care
Explanatory notes:
Additional economic and resource impact outcomes may include:
• time taken for assessment
• time taken to process diagnostic images by reporting practitioners, including additional reviews by specialists
• impact of technology on healthcare professional capacity
• impact on workload, e.g. numbers of biopsies, appointments and face-to-face appointments, and healthcare professional time

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of the economic and resource impact of using the DHT in the specified healthcare setting compared with standard care
Explanatory notes:
Additional economic and resource impact outcomes may include:
• time taken for administrative tasks
• time spent on review, with or without the AI technology
• costs associated with establishing and maintaining the infrastructure needed to implement the AI technologies, including software, hardware and staff training

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Outcomes should also be collected showing wider system level effects of using the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Relevant system-level outcomes may include but are not limited to:
• impact of using the technology on the care pathway
• impact of changes in treatments or service use after using the technologies
• impact of introducing the technologies on healthcare professionals' workload and administrative burden
• referral rates with and without DHT
• information about the impact on system indicators such as waiting times, number of people on waiting list and hospital capacity
• whether time savings translate into improvements in system efficiencies
• volume of procedures and utilisation of DHT

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the health problem including the clinical picture, severity and impact on people's daily lives and society
Explanatory notes: Include information on the clinical need and unmet need. Link to national priorities and policies, including how the DHT aligns with national health priorities and policy objectives

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the health problem including the clinical picture, severity and impact on people's daily lives and society
Explanatory notes:
Clearly state the indication for use supported by the technology's CE marking, classification, instructions for use and the International Classification of Diseases (ICD). If there are multiple indications, present each separately.
Describe any plans to seek reimbursement for new indications in the next 3 years. Include the provisional marketing schedule and any ongoing clinical investigations (with protocols, timetables and comparators).

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the health problem including the clinical picture, severity and impact on people's daily lives and society
Explanatory notes: Define and describe the target condition(s) using the International Classification of Diseases (ICD-10). Only use 3- or 4-digit codes and include an additional identifier (A, G, V, Z) if this is needed to determine the target user.

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Estimate the size of the target population and expected uptake and usage rates
Explanatory notes: Provide information on both the incidence (i.e. number of new cases) and the prevalence (i.e. total number of existing cases) of the target condition.

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Estimate the size of the target population and expected uptake and usage rates
Explanatory notes:
Where available, use relevant epidemiological studies to calculate the size of the target population. This should include prevalence, prevalence per subgroup (where applicable) and incidence per subgroup.
If no Belgian information is available, justify the extrapolation of data from other contexts to Belgium.

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Estimate the size of the target population and expected uptake and usage rates
Explanatory notes:
Define and quantify the proportion of people diagnosed with the target condition, including the proportion likely to be treated or monitored and the proportion likely to be treated or monitored remotely.
For each indication, describe the sources used for estimating the target population and how the estimate was derived. Use French data, but if this is not available the most recent international data should be used. State the type of data used (e.g. epidemiological study, database, clinical study etc.) and when and where the data was collected. If no data is available, you can estimate the target population size using predictive data.

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the current care pathway and standard treatment
Explanatory notes: Describe how the target condition is currently being treated or managed in the specified healthcare setting, including healthcare professional roles. This should be informed by relevant clinical experts and guidelines.

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the current care pathway and standard treatment
Explanatory notes:
Describe all treatment options that are currently considered standard care for the intended target population. Estimate the frequency (percentage) of how often each option is used in current practice.
Describe any new or emerging treatments (outside of the DHT) for the target condition that may not yet be routinely adopted as standard care. List any similar devices to the DHT, including the device name, company name and a description of the device.

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the proposed pathway using the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Describe where the DHT is intended to be used in the clinical pathway. This should include how people are referred to the technology and at what point in the pathway (e.g. self-referral without seeing a healthcare professional, referral by GP while on waiting list for specialist care, referral by healthcare professional to monitor post-treatment recovery, etc.).
Explain potential changes to the pathway related to the implementation of the DHT (e.g. displaced services, additional treatments etc.).

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the proposed pathway using the DHT
Explanatory notes: Provide a decision tree outlining the place of the DHT in the care pathway (e.g. symptom assessment, clinical assessment, diagnosis, treatment). Explain why the DHT should be used compared with existing alternatives.

HTA domain: Health problem and current use of the DHT
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Summarise the current use of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
State where the DHT is currently used, including countries and healthcare services. Clearly state if the DHT has not yet been launched and when this is expected.
Describe which user groups are currently using the technology and how it is being used (e.g. with healthcare professional support, unguided).
Provide published international recommendations and health technology assessments on the DHT.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clearly describe the DHT, including any associated components, accessories or variations in configuration
Explanatory notes:
Provide a clear description of the DHT and its intended use. This should include the device name, model, manufacturer, URL (where applicable) and the intended purpose of the technology (e.g. monitoring, treatment, diagnosis).
Where there are variations in DHT configuration or versions, differences must be clearly explained and rationalised. Describe any technology updates, including details of changes made since evidence generation.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clearly describe the DHT, including any associated components, accessories or variations in configuration
Explanatory notes:
Provide the notification number(s) of the device at the Federal Agency for Medicines and Health Products (FAMHP).
Provide a brochure, model or diagram describing the components of the DHT.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clearly describe the DHT, including any associated components, accessories or variations in configuration
Explanatory notes: Provide a diagram showing the components of the DHT, their purpose(s) and relationships.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: State whether the DHT is a single application or requires multiple applications
Explanatory notes:
Specify the type of application (e.g. mobile app, web app, or desktop program) and the software it is designed to run on.
If multiple applications exist, specify whether they are essential for the DHT to function.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the physical components and technical characteristics of the device
Explanatory notes: Physical component information should include weight, size, diameter and materials. If a battery is present, detail the expected battery life under various conditions of use, warranty period (with expiry date) and disposal procedures for the DHT post-use.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the physical components and technical characteristics of the device
Explanatory notes: Describe the composition of the packaging containing the DHT on the Belgian market.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide details on the network, performance and service characteristics of the DHT
Explanatory notes: Network and service characteristics include capacity, uptime, recovery time, restoration procedures, etc. Include assessments or documentation relating to scalability and load testing, ensuring these are aligned with expected or estimated uptake in practice.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe how users engage with the technology and how guidance is provided
Explanatory notes: Specify whether interaction with the DHT is passive, active or both. Provide a copy of the instructions for use, including different user versions (e.g. for healthcare professionals) where applicable.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe how the DHT supports remote monitoring and continuity of care
Explanatory notes: Detail the remote monitoring set-up (e.g. details of alerts, protocols, therapeutic support)

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe how the DHT supports remote monitoring and continuity of care
Explanatory notes:
For DHTs with remote medical monitoring, describe:
• remote monitoring functions (data collection, analysis, transmission; alerts with defined thresholds)
• data processing (collection, transmission and processing procedures; access methods; and procedures for correcting or deleting data)
• data type (physiological, clinical, psychological)
• user interfaces (patients, healthcare professionals)
• modules (e.g. messaging, import, export)
• data collected by the DHT
For each data element collection, explain why it is required.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: The DHT should be transparent and explainable
Explanatory notes: Describe explainability features (e.g. clear rationale for outputs, user-friendly explanations).

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Indicate the maturity and lifecycle stage of the technology
Explanatory notes:
Identify the lifecycle stage (preclinical, experimental or early validation, early clinical, comparative study, surveillance stage) and Technology readiness level of the DHT. Information on the ASSESS DHT lifecycle can be found in the ASSESS DHT PRISM tool.
Provide information on the lifespan of the DHT and accessories, including renewal frequency for hardware and software (where applicable). State any planned future updates and how the effects of these will be monitored.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
HTA dimension: Design and development of the technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Detail use of persuasive design elements and their suitability for the intended user group
Explanatory notes: Describe which persuasive design techniques are used and why these are appropriate for the target population, considering age, health condition and cultural factors.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
HTA dimension: Design and development of the technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of usability and user involvement in the design and testing of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Demonstrate compliance with relevant usability standards (e.g. ISO 62366-1, NHS DTAC D1).
Describe user involvement in design, development and testing of the DHT. Include evidence of usability testing with representative users and describe any actions taken in response to identified issues.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
HTA dimension: Design and development of the technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of usability and user involvement in the design and testing of the DHT
Explanatory notes: Demonstrate the DHT's usability in clinical practice in the specific country where it will be used, e.g. pilot studies, data from current use in the healthcare system.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
HTA dimension: Design and development of the technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe mechanisms for ongoing user feedback and technology improvements
Explanatory notes:
State how users can give feedback on the usability of the DHT. Explain feedback channels (e.g. in-app reporting, surveys) and response processes.
Outline how feedback informs continuous user experience and accessibility enhancements.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Information presented in the DHT should be valid, complete, scientifically supported and appropriate for the target population
Explanatory notes: Detail the source and quality of information, and provide content management plans for ensuring it remains accurate and up-to-date.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: The intervention delivered by the DHT should be appropriate for the target condition and intended purpose
Explanatory notes: Describe how the intervention aligns with the intended purpose. Where appropriate, describe the mode of action of the device in delivering treatment or intervention.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the degree to which the DHT can be personalised to meet individual user needs
Explanatory notes: Detail available personalisation features (e.g. adjustable settings, adaptive algorithms) and indicate how these features are relevant for diverse users.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the technical environment and operational dependencies required for safe and effective use of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Provide minimum hardware and software specifications for use of the DHT including:
• supported platforms and versions (e.g. Microsoft Windows, iOS, Android, OS X, Linux)
• device support list
• minimum hardware requirements for personal devices
• power supply and connectivity requirements (e.g. browser, network bandwidth)

Provide details of additional technologies required by healthcare professionals or patients to use the DHT effectively. Note any hardware or software dependencies, plug-ins or third-party integration required for the DHT to work as intended.
Outline potential access barriers for the target population (e.g. device availability, compatibility issues).

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the technical environment and operational dependencies required for safe and effective use of the DHT
Explanatory notes: If the patient is required to install the DHT on their personal device, state the percentage of the population that has a device that meets the minimum requirements for use.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clearly define installation, deployment and update processes
Explanatory notes:
Provide installation requirements and update processes.
Detail deployment requirements (installation steps, update mechanisms).
Explain any dependencies or prerequisites for successful operation.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: State any clinical procedures required for device placement and confirm compatibility of the device with medical imaging devices
Explanatory notes:
Describe any clinical procedures needed to place, fit, insert, implant, remove or replace the technology.
State the DHT's compatibility with medical imaging devices including magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), computed tomography (CT) and X-Ray.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Specify whether cloud platforms are used by the DHT and the contractual arrangements in place
Explanatory notes:
Identify cloud provider(s) and confirm whether the contract is direct or through an intermediary provider.
State regions or availability zones if this is relevant to data residency or performance.
Describe any additional cloud services necessary for the DHT to function, e.g. databases and analytics.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Specify whether cloud platforms are used by the DHT and the contractual arrangements in place
Explanatory notes: For DHTs with cloud storage, ensure that the use of the cloud platform complies with Belgian or European law.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a detailed overview of data requirements and data handling during deployment
Explanatory notes:
Detail required input data formats and standardisation needs (e.g. Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM), Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)).
Provide a full data dictionary describing expected fields, definitions and data types.
Detail quality thresholds, completeness requirements, and tolerance for missing or incorrect data or outliers.
Provide a full data flow map illustrating data ingestion, processing, storage and output.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate the ability of the DHT to use and exchange data with other information systems
Explanatory notes:
Demonstrate if and how collected data can be imported or exported into other clinical systems.
Explain supported data models and mapping frameworks.
Provide evidence that the DHT can export treatment-relevant data in both human-readable and interoperable machine-readable formats. Human-readable formats include PDF, plain text (TXT) and Microsoft Word (DOCX) formats. Machine-readable, interoperable formats include comma-separated values (CSV), JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) and Health Level Seven (HL7).
Describe any constraints or limitations on the reuse of collected data. Demonstrate that exports include all clinically relevant fields.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate the ability of the DHT to use and exchange data with other information systems
Explanatory notes: Demonstrate compliance with the Agence du Numérique en Santé (ANS)'s interoperability and security framework.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Specify the conditions and prerequisites for interoperability with other systems
Explanatory notes:
Detail technical requirements (network type, virtual private network (VPN) and authentication setup), dependencies on service providers, system versions or infrastructure components.
Detail exchange protocols and any constraints limiting interoperability (including licensing, proprietary formats and restricted access).

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Specify whether and how the DHT uses interfaces or APIs to access other software or services
Explanatory notes:
List application programming interfaces (APIs) used or provided (e.g. representational state transfer (REST) APIs, Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR) APIs) and provide details of any proprietary APIs if applicable.
Describe authentication and security mechanisms (e.g. OAuth 2.0, API keys) and identify any dependencies on third-party APIs or interfaces.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate successful interoperability with the clinical systems used in the intended deployment setting
Explanatory notes:
Show compatibility with electronic patient and health record systems and other clinical platforms.
Detail supported integration methods (e.g. Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM), Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR)).
Detail any additional infrastructure requirements or dependencies and demonstrate configuration steps required for deployment in local IT environments.
Describe how the DHT links with relevant local departments (e.g. IT, clinical engineering, procurement).

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate how the DHT connects with external devices and confirm compliance with relevant standards
Explanatory notes:
For wearables, sensors or other connected medical or wellness devices, provide information on connectivity and supported standards (e.g. ISO/IEEE 11073).
Detail data ingestion workflows and validation steps for device generated data.
Detail any hardware dependencies or proprietary integrations.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the types of data collected by the DHT and how the are processed, stored, exchanged, accessed and protected
Explanatory notes:
Information should include:
• types of data collected, e.g. personal, special category or health, device or telemetry, metadata
• parameters captured by the DHT, data flows and transmission types
• data collection methodologies, e.g. sensors, surveys, electronic health record integration, third‑party software development kits (SDKs)
• pre-processing steps for the data, e.g. cleansing, transformation, reduction and augmentation
• processing purposes and legal bases, e.g. care delivery, research, analytics, improvement
• storage locations and retention, e.g. on-device vs cloud, geography, encryption at rest
• data exchange mechanisms and standards, e.g. application programming interfaces (APIs), Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources (FHIR), secure file transfer, encryption in transit
• access controls and roles (who can access what, least-privilege, audit logs)
• privacy measures (pseudonymisation or anonymisation, differential privacy where applicable)

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Policies should be in place which govern the use of third-party software
Explanatory notes:
List third-party components (software development kits (SDKs), analytics, cloud providers and other vendors), purposes and data accessed (for each component).
Provide information on the opt-out mechanisms available to users related to third-party processing.
Provide a strategy for managing third-party update and vulnerability monitoring.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide information on account requirements and authentication measures, where applicable
Explanatory notes:
State whether registration and login are required to use the DHT, including whether guest or anonymous modes are offered.
Identity proofing level (none, email or SMS, government or health ID, face-to-face or remote verification).
Describe authentication methods (password, multi-factor authentication, passkeys, biometrics) and session management.
Provide information on account recovery and safeguards against takeover (rate limiting, lockouts, alerts).

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Users should be informed about data use and who is responsible for operation and governance of the DHT, including risk disclosures
Explanatory notes:
Provide evidence of user-facing notices regarding privacy information, rights and choices.
Provide a schedule of roles and responsibilities identifying the data controller, clinical safety officer, security officer and vendor contacts (if applicable).
Provide information on how changes are communicated and how preferences are managed.
Highlight channels available to users for queries and complaints and timelines for responses.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Operational security practices should be clearly explained and communicated
Explanatory notes: Provide incident response and review plans, patching and penetration testing cadence and information on disaster recovery plans.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Operational security practices should be clearly explained and communicated
Explanatory notes: Provide a technical eligibility criteria report.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Operational security practices should be clearly explained and communicated
Explanatory notes:
Demonstrate how the DHT complies with security requirements of the specific healthcare setting where it is intended to be used.
Describe training conducted by the developer or company to educate relevant personnel on security requirements and plans.
Outline procedures to support users and the healthcare setting in the event of a security incident, including how users will be informed of any known vulnerabilities.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a detailed description of the AI system, including datasets used and preprocessing methods
Explanatory notes:
Provide information on the datasets used for training, validation and testing, including assessment of their representativeness.
Provide information on preprocessing methods undertaken (e.g. normalisation, feature engineering and outlier handling), checks undertaken for data quality and bias before development of the model.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a detailed description of the AI system, including datasets used and preprocessing methods
Explanatory notes:
Describe the AI-based functionalities including:
• the role of each function
• the characteristics of the data used
• the result obtained
• how the algorithm works

Describe the samples used for initial training and relearning of the model, including demographics, size and composition. Describe how rare events have been considered.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a detailed description of the AI model type, learning approach and performance evaluation
Explanatory notes:
Include information on the learning type (e.g. supervised, unsupervised) and task (classification, regression) the AI is performing. Provide training and validation plans.
Describe how the performance of the model is evaluated (i.e. accuracy, precision, recall).
Outline performance metrics (e.g. area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC), root-mean-square deviation, F1-score, ZoneMap, Jaccard, factual fidelity, sensitivity and specificity) and thresholds for acceptable performance, with justification for how these thresholds were determined and validated. Include where appropriate hallucination and omission rates and healthcare professional edit/correction rates.
For generative language-based tools, provide evidence on performance for the language in the country where the technology is intended to be used, including specific regional dialects.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a detailed description of the AI model type, learning approach and performance evaluation
Explanatory notes: Describe how the algorithm was developed and who made it, including whether it relies on third-party services.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Clearly describe sources of input data used in decision-making once the AI is deployed
Explanatory notes:
This should include:
• variables involved in decisions and their characteristics (type, range, sensitivity, measurement units)
• sources of input data (patient-entered, sensor-derived, electronic health records integration)
• differences between training/validation/test data and real-world deployment data (e.g. environmental conditions, sensor variability)

Indicate how and where data was collected and any limitations.
Describe measures to detect and manage outlier data.

HTA domain: Description and technical characteristics of technology
Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate steps taken to identify and mitigate bias throughout the AI lifecycle
Explanatory notes: Describe bias risk assessment during design and planning, assessment of the representativeness of datasets, techniques for bias reduction in model training and evaluation, and post-deployment bias monitoring plans.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of regulatory conformity appropriate to the DHT's classification and intended use
Explanatory notes: Demonstrate conformity with medical device regulations (EU MDR) and provide information on regulatory status across relevant jurisdictions (e.g. CE marking/UK conformity assessed (UKCA)) with all associated certificates and declarations of conformity included.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of regulatory conformity appropriate to the DHT's classification and intended use
Explanatory notes: Demonstrate compliance with the EU Artificial Intelligence (AI) Act in line with the technology's risk classification.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence that the DHT has been registered with the appropriate regulatory agency (where appropriate)
Explanatory notes: Demonstrate that the DHT and company have been registered in the European Database on Medical Devices (EUDAMED) and the national regulatory agency in the country where the technology is being assessed (where applicable).

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of compliance with recognised security standards and demonstrate robust cybersecurity governance
Explanatory notes:
Relevant standards may include:
• ISO/IEC 27000 series - information security management
• OWASP Mobile application security verification standard (MASVS)
• IEC 82304‑1 - health software product safety
• ISO/IEEE 11073 series - medical device interoperability
• IEC 62304 - medical device software lifecycle
• ISO 13485 - medical device quality management
• ISO 14155 - clinical investigations
• ISO/TR 20416 - post‑market surveillance
• ISO 14971 - medical device risk management
Ensure compliance with appropriate country-specific standards for where the technology is intended to be used.

Provide documentation of security policies, including risk management strategies, patch management and vulnerability remediation, information classification policy, backup and recovery policy, and change management control.
Describe any adversarial, penetration or security testing undertaken and associated robustness measures.
Provide software bill of materials (SBOM) for third-party components.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide documentation demonstrating full compliance with applicable data protection laws and local information governance requirements
Explanatory notes:
Demonstrate compliance with relevant data protection and security criteria for countries where the technology is intended to be used (e.g. frameworks issued by France's Agence du Numérique en Santé (ANS), Germany's Digitale-Gesundheitsanwendungen-Verordnung (DiGAV), Finland's Digital health technology assessment (Digi-HTA) framework, UK's Digital Technology Assessment Criteria (DTAC)).
Demonstrate compliance with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), UK Data Protection Act 2018 (where relevant), or applicable national equivalents.
Provide a data protection impact assessment (DPIA).
Specify whether personal data is likely to be transferred outside the European Economic Area (EEA). If yes, identify destination countries, recipients and types of personal data transferred. State whether each transfer is covered by an applicable adequacy decision. Where it is not, describe the transfer mechanism and safeguards used, and provide any required transfer impact assessments (TIAs).
Provide a full description of data collection, processing, storage, retention and deletion policies across all DHT components.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide documentation demonstrating full compliance with applicable data protection laws and local information governance requirements
Explanatory notes: Complete the questionnaire in Annex 1 of the Digitale-Gesundheitsanwendungen-Verordnung (DiGAV) on data protection and information security as part of the electronic Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices (BfArM) application.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of any observed or reported undesirable effects, harms or safety‑related events associated with the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Provide evidence of any observed harms or safety events that have occurred from using the technology. Include reported incidents, adverse events, near misses, close calls, deviations or user-reported harms.
Present trends over time, and describe whether harms differ across settings, populations or use conditions.
Report product-related safety events from customer service or support logs where relevant.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of any observed or reported undesirable effects, harms or safety‑related events associated with the DHT
Explanatory notes: Submit a Periodic Safety Update Report (PSUR) where available summarising post-market safety data. If a PSUR is not available, provide a quantitative overview of reported incidents associated with the use of the DHT in Belgium and other countries. For each reported incident, state the type of incident, source and action taken.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of any observed or reported undesirable effects, harms or safety‑related events associated with the DHT
Explanatory notes: State the person in the company who is responsible for submitting Manufacturing Incident Reports to the Finnish Medicines Agency (Fimea).

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of any observed or reported undesirable effects, harms or safety‑related events associated with the DHT
Explanatory notes: Summarise medical device vigilance data on the DHT from France and other countries over the past 5 years. This should include the number of units sold, number of reported adverse events or malfunctions, serious incidents, incident rate and cumulative incident rate. Provide an analysis of incidents that have impacted the availability or correct operation of the DHT.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe all known and potential risks associated with using the DHT, supported by study results where available
Explanatory notes:
Provide information on potential adverse outcomes that could occur from the implementation and use of the technology. This could include:
• risks directly related to the DHT itself (e.g. usability risks, algorithmic risks, device connectivity failures)
• risks linked to user behaviour (misuse, non‑compliance, misunderstanding of outputs)
• risks related to treatment or care delivery (e.g. misinterpretation of prompts, delays from workflow disruptions)

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Identify populations at greater risk of harm and specify user groups or conditions where the DHT may be unsuitable
Explanatory notes:
Provide information on any identified vulnerable groups with a higher likelihood of adverse effects.
Detail contraindications and conditions in which the DHT should not be used.
Detail environment-specific risks (e.g. unsupervised home use vs use supervised by a healthcare professional).
Indicate any contexts where the DHT should not be used.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a comparative safety analysis between the DHT and current standard care
Explanatory notes:
Compare rates and types of adverse events, workflow risks or unintended consequences.
Highlight whether harms increase, decrease or change in nature compared to standard practice.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: For DHTs with diagnostic or prognostic functionality, assess and report the safety impact of error types
Explanatory notes:
Report false positives, negatives and incidental findings.
Detail how diagnostic error rates compare with standard practice.
Describe the potential risks to clinical decision making and care associated with diagnostic errors.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Explain measures taken to reduce safety risks particularly where vulnerable users or peer‑to‑peer interactions are involved
Explanatory notes:
Detail mitigation strategies for known risks, and controls in place to prevent misuse and unsafe reliance on the DHT.
Demonstrate design features that promote safe use of the DHT, and training and onboarding materials that reduce risk.
Provide safeguarding assurances, particularly where vulnerable users or peer‑to‑peer interactions are involved.
Describe controls governing who can access the platform, including details of user privileges and suitability checks.
Detail measures in place to ensure safe interaction including moderation processes for user-generated content or community features (if applicable).
Describe the processes and infrastructure for identifying and responding to safeguarding concerns and safety-related events, including escalation routes and reporting mechanisms.
Detail additional protections in place for vulnerable users.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Explain measures taken to reduce safety risks particularly where vulnerable users or peer‑to‑peer interactions are involved
Explanatory notes:
Describe how information on patient and device safety is communicated to users. This should include whether and how potential users are informed of:
• groups and indications that should not use the technology
• risks and measures to mitigate or avoid risks
• when to consult a healthcare professional
• when to stop using the technology
• errors in the DHT

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Identify and describe all risks related to the technical stability, performance and reliability of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Detail risks arising from system instability, outages or degraded performance; and loss, corruption or bias in clinical information.
Detail risks associated with loss of privacy, confidentiality and user reputation; and reliability and repeatability of data capture and processing.
Provide information on handling of measurement bias, data quality issues and resilience under stress conditions.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a post‑deployment monitoring and governance plan for the DHT, including quality monitoring processes and continuous improvement of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Detail expected performance changes over time. Provide information on the monitoring of usage patterns and performance.
Detail governance arrangements and independent oversight mechanisms for change management and any triggers for corrective actions or re-evaluation of the DHT. Detail quality assurance processes for permanent performance upgrades.
Describe mechanisms in place that verify the DHT remains clinically useful, safe and aligned with its intended purpose.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a post‑deployment monitoring and governance plan for the DHT, including quality monitoring processes and continuous improvement of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Describe the model update regimen and whether this is initial, incremental or continuous.
Provide expected sources of retraining data, including methods for ensuring data quality and representativeness.
Demonstrate tools for monitoring model performance, degradation, bias and performance drift.
Detail protocols for tracing, archiving and analysing degradations and corrective action plans.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a post‑deployment monitoring and governance plan for the DHT, including quality monitoring processes and continuous improvement of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Describe the company's testing process and how error messages are handled.
Describe whether the DHT can be rolled back to an earlier version when needed.
Provide information on how the performance of the DHT is monitored to automatically identify faults and technical issues.
Describe the process for decommissioning the DHT. State whether there has been any downtime or impairment time in the past 6 months and why.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide an end‑to‑end risk management system aligned with recognised medical device standards
Explanatory notes:
Confirm whether the DHT has undergone a formal risk analysis, and that risk management policy is aligned with relevant standards (e.g. ISO 14971).
Provide risk analysis reports, including hazard identification, mitigation and risk justification.
Provide safety documentation that covers all components of data collection, handling and transmission.
Provide documentation of fallback modes, safe failure behaviour and continuity of care safeguards.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Identify any risks the DHT poses to the environment during development, deployment or routine use
Explanatory notes:
Examples of environmental safety risks include:
• increased emissions from manufacturing, packaging or transporting devices
• excessive freshwater consumption for cooling AI data centres
• electronic waste from obsolete sensors, wearables, batteries etc.
• high electricity consumption by data centres, cloud computing, AI training etc.

Describe how environmental risks are/will be mitigated.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of the DHT’s carbon footprint and greenhouse gas emissions, including any environmental impact assessment
Explanatory notes:
This may include:
• a product carbon footprint or lifecycle assessment
• carbon reports and energy-source data
• an independently verified environmental impact assessment or audit
• plans for reducing emissions

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the raw materials, energy consumption, and waste generated in the development, deployment, and lifecycle of the DHT.
Consider the overall body of evidence supporting the use of the DHT in the relevant clinical setting
Explanatory notes:
Evidence on the DHT can be demonstrated through several sources including clinical studies. These should be high-quality and appropriate to capturing the relative benefits and harms of using the DHT.
At a minimum, evidence should be relevant and applicable to the specific country and healthcare setting and show:
• non-inferiority of the clinical effectiveness of the DHT compared with current standard care
• clinical improvement in the target condition using standardised measures currently used in the relevant healthcare setting
• impact on health-related quality of life
• longer-term clinical and resource-use impacts of the DHT to the healthcare service
• impact on the care pathway including referrals, workload and costs associated with its implementation
• user engagement with the DHT including intervention acceptance, usability, experiences, completion rates and uptake rates in different subpopulations where applicable
• cost or time-savings associated with the DHT
• safe use of the technology including all adverse events

Input on evidence generation and study design should be obtained from clinical and research experts and people with lived experience where needed.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Consider the overall body of evidence supporting the use of the DHT in the relevant clinical setting
Explanatory notes:
Minimum evidence provided should also show:
• the diagnostic accuracy and failure rates of the technology compared with standard care
• accuracy of the technology in relevant subgroups
• clinical and service outcomes

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Consider the overall body of evidence supporting the use of the DHT in the relevant clinical setting
Explanatory notes: Minimum evidence should demonstrate implementation of the DHT (1) as an autonomous tool and (2) with healthcare professional review. This will aid understanding of how effective the technology is when used in routine practice

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide high‑quality evidence comparing the DHT to relevant alternatives
Explanatory notes:
It is important to provide independent, externally reviewed research, e.g. studies not authored by or affiliated with the company. Peer-reviewed publications are preferred due to their independent assessment of quality.
Data could be collected using a combination of:
• primary data collection, e.g. adequately powered, high-quality clinical studies
• suitable real-world data sources, e.g. national clinical databases
• data collected through the technology itself, e.g. usage data, number of referrals, diagnostic outcomes predicted by the DHT
• post-market surveillance activities done by the technology developer. This may include data relating to the number of referrals seen, or the proportion of outcomes or performance data for the technology in comparison with a pre-defined ground truth.

Acceptable types and levels of evidence may vary by HTA agency and country. In general, high-quality randomised controlled trials (RCTs) are preferred over non-randomised or observational studies. Check with the specific agency doing the assessment to confirm their evidence requirements.
Other acceptable study designs may include: comparative cohort studies, case-control studies, real-world historical control studies with propensity score methods, real-world before-and-after implementation studies, validation studies, matched cohort studies, company evaluation studies, real-world database studies, economic studies, prospective audit, systematic reviews, meta-analyses.
If an interventional study was/is not feasible, justify the alternative study design used.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide high‑quality evidence comparing the DHT to relevant alternatives
Explanatory notes: Data on starting therapy and engagement metrics may be generated through the technology itself. This can be integrated with routinely collected datasets where appropriate.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide high‑quality evidence comparing the DHT to relevant alternatives
Explanatory notes:
Most data, particularly relating to diagnostic accuracy, is likely best collected through primary data collection.
A retrospective study design may be appropriate for assessing diagnostic accuracy. But prospective evidence will better show the impact of the technologies on other outcomes, such as changes to clinical management.
Acceptable study designs may include: retrospective diagnostic accuracy studies, prospective diagnostic accuracy studies, before-and-after studies, economic studies, real-world before-and-after implementation study, cross-sectional diagnostic accuracy study, retrospective service-evaluation study.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide high‑quality evidence comparing the DHT to relevant alternatives
Explanatory notes:
A possible study design is an experimental concordance study assessing the concordance between the diagnoses reached for each included case by the: (1) healthcare professional assisted by the DHT (intervention), (2) healthcare professional unassisted by the DHT (comparator), and (3) reference standard. Consider also collecting data on the diagnostic accuracy of the technology alone as this can provide a lower bound to identify drift from intended use because of automation bias.
Note that for some DHTs, retrospective studies may not fully capture the diagnostic accuracy of using the technology with healthcare professional review in clinical practice. This is because healthcare professionals in retrospective studies typically perform this task in isolation and not with the patient or case notes as they would in clinical practice.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide high‑quality evidence comparing the DHT to relevant alternatives
Explanatory notes:
Clinical data may include recommendations for good practice, technology assessment reports, and organisational impact studies.
The following types of evidence cannot be used to support claims of relative benefits of the DHT: theses, perspective or editorial articles, articles in languages other than English or French, and letters of recommendation from experts.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide high‑quality evidence comparing the DHT to relevant alternatives
Explanatory notes:
Minimum evidence for listing in the directory is a retrospective comparative study. Higher levels of evidence such as a prospective comparative study can also be submitted.
Examples of accepted study designs include case-control studies, cohort studies, before-and-after studies, non-randomised or randomised controlled trials. Other possible study designs include pragmatic clinical trials, sequential multiple assignment randomised trial or multiphase optimisation strategy.
The following types of evidence cannot be used to support claims of a positive healthcare effect: evidence based solely on expert opinion or reports, case reports, case series, cross-sectional studies.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Assess the benefits of using the DHT through robust quantitative methods, and provide qualitative evidence capturing user experience and perceptions of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Quantitative evidence may include experimental clinical trials, observational studies or modelling.
Qualitative evidence may include surveys, interviews or case studies involving patients and healthcare professionals. Qualitative studies should: explore user experience, engagement and barriers to access; include reported outcomes (acceptability, usability and preferences) from people using the technologies; and include a broad and inclusive distribution of eligible users who are representative of the population of potential users.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate real-world performance and relevance to standard or best practice
Explanatory notes:
Evidence may include pilot studies, service evaluations or implementation reports. Demonstrate alignment with real-world settings and clearly state any anticipated or observed operational constraints. Evidence from pilot sites may be used to confirm the benefits of the DHT with regard to acceptability, performance and integration into care pathways.
Refer to the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE)'s real-world evidence framework for guidance on planning, conducting and reporting on real-world evidence studies.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate real-world performance and relevance to standard or best practice
Explanatory notes:
Examples of real-world data sources include:
• Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA)'s clinical practice research datalink
• NHS England's hospital episode statistics
• NHS England's Emergency Care Data Set
• NHS England Secure Data Environment

Examples of real-world data sources for specific conditions include:
• The Osteoarthritis Initiative
• NHS England's Diagnostic Imaging Dataset
• NHS picture archiving and communication system
• The Fracture Liaison Service Database
• The Diagnostic Imaging Dataset
• The National Joint Registry
• NHS England's national patient-reported outcome measures programme
• The NHS Talking Therapies for anxiety and depression and Mental Health Services Data Set
• NHS England's National Cancer Registration and Analysis Service
• The National Disease Registration Service
• The National Audit of Cardiac Rehabilitation
• National Institute for Cardiovascular Outcomes Research
• National Cardiac Audit Programme

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide, where available and appropriate, expert perspectives on use and implementation of the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Some (but not all) HTA agencies may consider expert perspectives in their assessment of the DHT. Check with the specific agency doing the assessment to confirm whether they accept this type of evidence.
Where accepted, provide any expert advice, clinical opinion or unpublished data where higher-order evidence is limited. For example, expert elicitation may be used to supplement evidence when resource use data is limited or uncertain.
Evidence of support from patient associations or professional bodies may also be provided, but ensure this is clearly contextualised.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide, where available and appropriate, expert perspectives on use and implementation of the DHT
Explanatory notes: Expert advice is considered the lowest level of evidence and will not carry significant weight in the assessment. For each item of expert advice, clearly state the name, title, institution and potential conflicts of interest with particular attention to the relationship with the company.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Evidence should be high quality and low in bias
Explanatory notes:
Ensure steps have been taken to produce reliable results, with bias either mitigated or avoided.
Demonstrate that study data is methodologically robust, and there is high certainty in the performance of the DHT.
Data collection should follow a predefined protocol.
Quality assurance processes should be put in place to ensure the integrity and consistency of data collection.
Eligibility criteria should be clearly defined and consistent across groups in the study to minimise selection bias.
Non-random assignment to intervention or comparison groups introduces a risk of confounding bias. Appropriate methods such as matching or adjustment should be used to minimise bias and balance confounding factors between groups. Experts should be consulted during protocol development to help identify key confounders.
Data from intervention and comparison groups should be collected at appropriate time intervals including clearly defined follow-ups.
Issues with data quality such as incomplete records and demographically imbalanced groups may impact analysis. Clear reporting about data quality is important and approaches such as multiple imputation could be used to address issues.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Evidence should provide clear and detailed information on the intervention, patient groups, comparators and outcomes
Explanatory notes:
This should include:
• individual characteristics at baseline to support subgroup analyses and adjustment for confounding, and to demonstrate whether the DHT has been tested or validated in diverse patient groups
• details of standard care including which healthcare professionals were involved and which additional treatments or medicines were offered
• detailed descriptions of the technologies including their training requirements, specific products and versions, and any optional features that are being used (including any artificial intelligence add-ons for program selection)

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate that the available evidence is relevant to the target population and intended indication(s)
Explanatory notes:
Evidence should be in a setting that is relevant to the health and care system of the country conducting the assessment. Companies should involve clinical experts from the intended country of use in the design and running of studies to ensure that populations, intervention delivery and comparators are relevant to the specific country and setting. Justify relevance where study populations differ from the target population. For transdiagnostic DHTs or those indicated across multiple conditions, provide evidence in the population defined in scope.
For some conditions, the care pathway and standard care differ across countries making studies done in other countries less applicable. For evidence generated in different countries or settings, companies should consider whether it is transferable to the current assessment setting, e.g. does it reflect the care pathway, treatment delivery, patient population, healthcare professional roles and banding, etc. Where applicable, evidence should be provided supporting the transferability of evidence to the intended use case.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe all ongoing or planned studies evaluating the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Provide registration details and protocols where available. Describe how scheduled changes or updates to the DHT are addressed in the protocol.
State the indication(s) and objectives of each study, study design (e.g. interventional, observational, feasibility), number of participants, and study timelines including start and anticipated closing dates.
Describe plans for ongoing data collection during routine use of the DHT.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe all ongoing or planned studies evaluating the DHT
Explanatory notes: Provide an Excel sheet listing all ongoing clinical studies on the DHT, including study title, indication, expected number of participants, type of study, expected length of follow-up, expected timeline for completion and registry details.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe all ongoing or planned studies evaluating the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Demonstrate that ongoing or planned studies will provide sufficient evidence to support the application for reimbursement of the DHT, considering the type of study, study objectives, target population, study timelines and data analysis plans.
Where possible, describe unpublished data from ongoing studies supported by an accepted manuscript.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe all ongoing or planned studies evaluating the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Studies must be registered in a primary or partner registry of the World Health Organisation International Clinical Trials Registry Platform. The primary registry for Germany is the German Register of Clinical Studies (DRKS) at the BfArM.
Provide an evaluation concept produced by an independent (i.e. not associated with the company) scientific institute. This should include the study protocol, study design, the choice of outcomes and comparator(s), a description of clinical practice in the relevant healthcare system, and how the study will provide evidence of the intended positive healthcare effect.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide study protocol(s) and statistical analysis plans, where appropriate
Explanatory notes:
Include full protocol and statistical analysis plan for studies on the DHT where appropriate.
Explain outcome measures, analysis methods and handling of missing data.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Explain how changes to the DHT are managed in relation to the evidence base and regulatory classification
Explanatory notes:
Describe differences between the current version of the DHT and versions evaluated in studies.
Detail the nature of changes (minor, secondary component or major technological modifications).
Provide evidence of clinical equivalence between versions where applicable.
Where major changes affect performance, safety, intended use or data interpretation, submit new evidence for the assessed version.
Reference applicable regulatory requirements (e.g. Regulation (EU) 2017/745, Annex VIII rule 11).

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence showing that the DHT can plausibly achieve one or more positive health effects for a clearly defined patient group
Explanatory notes:
Specify the target patient group and clinical context.
Describe the mechanisms by which the DHT is expected to produce healthcare benefits.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence showing that the DHT can plausibly achieve one or more positive health effects for a clearly defined patient group
Explanatory notes: Decision makers may consider evidence of clinical benefit of the non-digital intervention on which the DHT was based (e.g. paper-based intervention). This should be supported by evidence showing the equivalence of the digital and non-digital versions of the intervention.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence showing that the DHT can plausibly achieve one or more positive health effects for a clearly defined patient group
Explanatory notes: Demonstrate at least one positive healthcare effect. This can be a medical benefit or patient-relevant improvement of structure and process. This must align with the technology's intended use, functions, content and manufacturing materials.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of the benefits of the DHT relative to current care, including uncertainty
Explanatory notes:
Explain how the DHT improves outcomes or care delivery beyond existing solutions. Claims must be based on impact rather than incremental technical features. Consider risks associated with use of the DHT and how these compare with anticipated benefits.
Compare clinical and organisational benefits of the DHT against standard care or existing alternatives. Quantify benefits where possible (e.g. confidence intervals, scenario ranges). Discuss assumptions underlying benefit estimates.
Clearly identify any uncertainty associated with figures presented as part of the evidence base. Uncertainty should be quantified (e.g. confidence intervals or probability distribution).

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Evaluate the impact of the DHT on health outcomes and wider system-level effects
Explanatory notes:
Demonstrate the following:
• health benefits (e.g. clinical outcomes, quality of life)
• impacts on system efficiency, resource use and care pathways
• structural or procedural effects on service delivery
• anticipated outcomes compared with current practice
