Provide evidence on long-term follow-up showing the effects of the DHT after use. Longer-term economic evidence or modelling may be needed to fully capture the DHT's benefits and costs.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide an overall summary and synthesis of the evidence base and its implications
Explanatory notes:
Provide a comprehensive list of published and unpublished studies, clearly stating which version of the DHT was used in each study. HTA reports and recommendations may also be submitted. Unpublished data may be included, provided that limitations are clearly stated.
Provide an overview of study results relevant to clinical outcomes and improvements in care delivery. Evidence synthesis (with sensitivity analysis) may be used if there are several studies. Where multiple study types exist, prioritise conclusions based on the highest level of evidence.
Clearly state the strength of evidence in relation to claims made for the DHT. Highlight consistency or divergence across studies. Identify remaining evidence gaps and how they will be addressed.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide an overall summary and synthesis of the evidence base and its implications
Explanatory notes:
Provide an Excel sheet listing all studies on the DHT that are relevant to the intended use case. For each study, clearly state the study title, number of participants, type of study, follow-up period and registry details. 
Provide full-text study reports or publications where available.
Provide a general summary of studies, including inclusion criteria and conclusion from all publications. Secondary assessment criteria should only be discussed if the primary assessment criteria showed significant and clinically relevant results.
Provide a systematic literature review on the use of the DHT compared with standard care (where applicable). The review should be conducted no more than 6 months before the application is submitted. If there is no evidence on the DHT, describe how the broader literature applies to the technology. Search results should be presented in a flow diagram in line with established conventions of reporting. The review should not include abstracts or conference presentations, documents not in the national language or English and letters of recommendation from experts.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide an overall summary and synthesis of the evidence base and its implications
Explanatory notes: State whether any institution (such as the Duodecim Current Care Guidelines or an HTA agency in another country) has recommended the DHT, supported by the name of the institution and the accompanying recommendation or report.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide an overall summary and synthesis of the evidence base and its implications
Explanatory notes: Summarise relevant studies in tables that should include the type of study, date and duration of study, study aims, methods and results. For methods, describe participant selection criteria, scope of the study, location, details of the intervention, primary and secondary endpoints, sample size calculation, randomisation and data analysis. For results, report the number of participants, patient characteristics and comparability of groups, findings related to the primary and secondary endpoints, and adverse events.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide an overall summary and synthesis of the evidence base and its implications
Explanatory notes:
Submit a systematic evaluation of data on the use of the DHT. This should include a systematic literature review and a systematic evaluation and analysis of data generated from the use of the DHT. Report the number of participants, recruitment methods, outcome measures, intervention effects, etc.
The systematic review should detail the search strategy including the search period, sources, and search terms used. Sources should include relevant international bibliographic databases. Search results should be presented in a flow diagram in line with established conventions of reporting.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide up-to-date costs and resource use estimates associated with current practice
Explanatory notes:
Provide all direct and relevant indirect costs associated with current practice. Cost data should be current and up-to-date. Estimates should use country‑specific pricing, resource tariffs, data sources and cost units. Use national reference costs, published tariffs or validated local datasets where possible.
Explain applicability to different user groups, service contexts or delivery models.
Document all assumptions and their justification.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide clear and complete information on the costs of using the DHT in the specified healthcare setting. Detail the pricing model for the DHT and all associated costs required for effective use
Explanatory notes:
Costs should reflect the use case in the clinical evidence and the intended use in clinical practice. Provide up-to-date direct and indirect costs associated with using the DHT in clinical practice. This should include:
• the average and minimum price of the DHT
• the distribution method
• any in-app purchases, subscription fees and usage-based charges as well as any discounts
• cost of any accessories, devices, sensors or peripherals
• cost of services necessary for the DHT to function (e.g. assessment appointments, infrastructure)
• training costs

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide clear and complete information on the costs of using the DHT in the specified healthcare setting. Detail the pricing model for the DHT and all associated costs required for effective use
Explanatory notes:
Provide the average and minimum price, excluding VAT, of the DHT and associated accessories recorded over the last 3 years.
Provide sales volumes and 3-year sales forecasts of the DHT for the intended use case, including the number of users and monthly packages per year.
State the expected duration of using the DHT and associated accessories.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe current or expected resource use resulting from implementation of the DHT compared with standard care
Explanatory notes: Ensure estimates of resource use are based on clinical practice, e.g. from clinical trial data, real-world evidence, routinely collected health system data and expert opinion.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide information on existing reimbursements of the DHT
Explanatory notes: Describe any existing reimbursements of the DHT, including reimbursements in other countries. Include the nature of possible reimbursements, ongoing or completed applications for reimbursement and the status of these applications.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide comparative analysis showing how the DHT affects costs and resource use relative to current standard practice
Explanatory notes: State the evidence source for each comparison (study, model, real‑world data) and detail cost offsets or new costs introduced by the DHT.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide comparative analysis showing how the DHT affects costs and resource use relative to current standard practice
Explanatory notes:
Describe the expected costs and savings at the national level when treating all expected patients.
Provide a budget impact analysis for the first year of using the DHT. Calculations should be easily explained and repeatable. Provide an Excel file with the calculations clearly showing the input values and formulas used.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Explore and quantify uncertainty in all cost and resource‑use estimates
Explanatory notes:
Use sensitivity analyses by varying key assumptions (e.g. adherence rates, event rates, cost inputs) and present ranges, confidence intervals or probability distributions.
Highlight how uncertainty affects comparative cost‑effectiveness or budget impact.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the infrastructure, services and organisational components needed to implement the DHT
Explanatory notes:
List required physical and digital infrastructure (servers, networks, secure environments, clinical workstations).
Detail local support needed for installation and configuration, and provisions for monitoring.
Note any dependencies on existing health and care systems.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the infrastructure, services and organisational components needed to implement the DHT
Explanatory notes:
For robotics, describe any changes to existing infrastructure for the implementation and use of the technology, e.g. elevator control systems, changes to building floor plans etc.
Outline any arrangements needed to teach or programme the robot to operate within the healthcare setting.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe the technical assistance and maintenance arrangements required to operate the DHT safely and reliably
Explanatory notes:
Detail preventative and corrective maintenance schedules, and support channels available for users.
Note processes for equipment recovery, decommissioning and waste disposal of the DHT.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe all training, education and experience required for healthcare professionals to use the DHT safely and effectively
Explanatory notes:
Provide training and support plans for healthcare professionals. This should include who needs training, who provides training, length of training and costs.
If there is an expected learning curve with your DHT (i.e. outcomes improve with more time or experience using the technology), describe how the analysis accounts for this learning curve and how this may differ when used in routine practice. Consider whether the learning curve may extend beyond formal training and how this may impact clinical outcomes and efficiencies.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide details on training or support required for patients to use the DHT as intended
Explanatory notes: Provide training and support plans for patients and/or carers. Include options for people who do not have the required digital skills or technical equipment.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Detail the terms and conditions of use for patients and healthcare professionals.
Define the role of each healthcare professional involved in the implementation and ongoing use of the DHT
Explanatory notes: This should include strategies to help healthcare providers communicate the outputs, key features, benefits and limitations of the DHT to patients.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Specify the role of patients and/or carers in the implementation and use of the DHT, including requirements and responsibilities
Explanatory notes:
Describe the digital skills (e.g. installing apps, using sensors) and technical equipment required for patients.
Define expectations for adherence, data entry or self‑monitoring.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Specify the level of professional oversight when used in practice
Explanatory notes: This should be proportionate to the risk associated with failure of the DHT to perform as expected.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe potential changes to the delivery of care according to the different stakeholders involved in the provision of care, including indirect impacts related to changes to treatment
Explanatory notes:
Describe expected changes to the delivery of care and distribution of tasks, impacts on workload (increase, decrease, redeployment) and indirect impacts on treatment pathways or clinical processes.
Detail implications for service capacity, triage, monitoring and escalation.
Demonstrate alignment with existing pathways and any required pathway modifications.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence clearly demonstrating the organisational benefits provided by the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Evidence should be from research assessing healthcare professional experience and organisational outcomes associated with the DHT.
Include results of any organisational impact studies or evaluations, and explain how these results informed key decisions in the development and deployment of the DHT.
Demonstrate efficiency gains or improvements in service delivery using relevant data (both quantitative and qualitative).
Provide evidence of benefits perceived or experienced by healthcare professionals and patient- or system-level outcomes.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence clearly demonstrating the organisational benefits provided by the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Provide a detailed impact analysis.
Use Haute Autorité de Santé (HAS)'s organisational impact map to demonstrate the impact of the DHT on (1) the care process, (2) the skills and abilities of those involved in the care process and (3) society or the community. Describe how this impact is defined and measured, and whether it is expected on an individual or collective scale.
Where applicable, identify the organisations involved in generating evidence or providing expert opinion on the organisational impact of using the DHT.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of the broader impact of the DHT beyond individual users and the organisation
Explanatory notes:
Describe the impact of the DHT on the wider system, such as its potential to address unmet needs.
Support claims with data from good practice recommendations, clinical studies, modelling or published evaluations.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of the broader impact of the DHT beyond individual users and the organisation
Explanatory notes: Where applicable, describe the impact of the DHT on society and the community, ensuring that claims of significant benefits are supported by data.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of patients' perceived benefits of the DHT on health or quality of life
Provide information on people who stopped using the DHT and why
Explanatory notes:
Describe the proportion of people who stopped using the DHT, including patient demographics and characteristics such as digital literacy and experience.
State whether discontinuation of use may be related to safety concerns or adverse events.
Include data comparing use and discontinuation rates for the DHT and standard care

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of real-world usability and user feedback mechanisms
Explanatory notes:
Include results from pilots, user feedback, and any identified barriers or enablers to use.
Evaluate how well users interact with and use the technology, including any difficulties related to its implementation or use in clinical practice.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe any information or strategies to ensure appropriate use of the DHT and increased adherence
Explanatory notes: Provide any guides or advice that should be followed or communicated to users to facilitate use of the DHT.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe measures for consumer protection and support
Explanatory notes: Describe any measures to be consumer-friendly and to support users. Detail consumer-friendly terms, in-app purchase protections, service-level agreements, response times, etc.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe how information on the DHT's purpose, functionality and limitations is transparently communicated to users
Explanatory notes:
Demonstrate steps taken to provide users with clear and correct information on the DHT, including how it works, user roles and responsibilities, data collection and storage, and potential risks associated with use.
Detail informed consent processes, aligned with General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and national data protection laws.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe how information on the DHT's purpose, functionality and limitations is transparently communicated with users
Explanatory notes:
Describe autonomy safeguards to ensure users understand system outputs and maintain control over decisions. State human oversight mechanisms for critical decisions.
Describe algorithmic functions transparently, appropriate to classification and intellectual property limitations.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide an equality impact assessment on using the DHT in the relevant healthcare setting
Explanatory notes:
This should evaluate potential equality and equity issues associated with the implementation and use of the DHT in the specific healthcare setting, including steps taken to address these issues in the design, development, and implementation of the technology. It may include any additional support, training or accommodations that increase access and help reduce exclusion of specific groups.
Provide evidence on the use and uptake of the DHT within the relevant healthcare setting, including the number of people who decline, are not offered or are not eligible to use the technology.
Provide evidence on outcomes in subgroups who may be less likely to be offered or to use the DHT.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe any potential equality issues relating to the target condition and how these have been considered for the DHT
Explanatory notes: Describe whether the target condition disproportionately affects particular population groups and how this has been considered in the design, development, implementation and evidence generation activities (including participant recruitment, retention, intervention delivery etc.). Consider relevant protected characteristics including age; disability; gender reassignment; marriage or civil partnership status; pregnancy and maternity; race including colour, nationality, ethnic or national origin; religion or belief; sex or sexual orientation.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Demonstrate that participants in the evidence reflect the diversity of the target population
Explanatory notes:
The evidence should be representative of the intended target population, clinical setting and mode of delivery of the DHT. Consider whether important population groups are appropriately represented in the evidence, particularly relevant subgroups such as people who:
• may not be able to attend in-person appointments
• stop using the technology
• are disabled or have accessibility needs
• are less comfortable with digital technologies or have limited access to the internet or smart devices
• have significant comorbidities
Consider which population characteristics are most relevant for your DHT. State whether important patient groups are underrepresented in the evidence and why.

Describe measures taken to minimise selection bias and support inclusive recruitment of participants. Consider whether additional support, accommodations or alternative study approaches including consideration of cultural, language or digital literacy needs were required to facilitate participation for specific groups. Involve relevant clinical and patient experts in evidence planning and generation to ensure representative recruitment.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Describe how the DHT may increase access to care within the relevant healthcare system
Explanatory notes:
Describe how the technology may improve access to healthcare services, for example through a potential reduction in waiting times; increased engagement, attendance or completion of treatment; or increased access to services that would not otherwise be available (e.g. by providing remote care to people who may otherwise be unable to access in-person services).
Provide evidence of any specific subgroups that may especially benefit (or not benefit) from using the DHT.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Identify barriers to accessing and using the DHT and describe how these can be mitigated
Explanatory notes:
Outline any potential barriers people may face when trying to access or use the DHT. This may include language or communication barriers, low digital literacy, limited access to devices etc. Consider also the potential for the DHT to increase barriers to care in the target population such as geographical variation in service availability, digital exclusion or inaccessible referral pathways.
Describe any specific groups who may have difficulty accessing or using the DHT and how this has been considered and mitigated in implementation and evidence generation. This may include people:
• with neurodiverse conditions
• with a learning disability
• with a visual, hearing or cognitive impairment
• who have difficulty reading, writing or understanding health-related information
• with problems with manual dexterity

Describe any specific steps that can be taken to increase access, inclusion and engagement (e.g. training and support, alternative delivery routes, language adaptations).

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence showing continuity of care provided by the DHT
Explanatory notes:
Provide evidence that use of the DHT does not result in unintended gaps, delays or discontinuities in care.
Describe arrangements for ensuring the quality and continuity of care provided by the DHT, especially for users with reduced access or digital literacy barriers.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide a description of how accessibility has been considered in the design of the DHT
Explanatory notes: Describe how accessibility requirements were incorporated into the design, development and delivery of the DHT to support use by people with a range of accessibility needs. This may include text formatting and layout, screen magnification and screen-reader compatibility.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide information on accessibility conformance and platform features
Explanatory notes: Where applicable, provide evidence of accessibility testing, certification, audits or formal assessments (e.g. WCAG 2.1, VoiceOver/TalkBack).

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide information on accessibility conformance and platform features
Explanatory notes: Describe the accessibility features supported by your DHT (e.g. VoiceOver, Dynamic Type, TalkBack, Select to Speak). Include how the technology follows design guidelines for the specific platform (e.g. iOS or Android).

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of how special user groups were considered or involved in product design
Explanatory notes:
Describe how users with specific accessibility needs were involved in the design of the DHT. This may include people who:
• have visual impairments
• use a screen reader
• are colour blind
• have hearing impairments or use sign language
• are non-native language speakers
• have cognitive challenges (such as perception, memory, learning challenges)
• have fine motor difficulties
• have epilepsy

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide evidence of accessibility assessment or testing
Explanatory notes: Describe any accessibility assessment or testing undergone by the DHT. Include details of the type of testing and who performed it. Provide evaluation documents where possible.

Overarching Evidence Recommendation: Provide the accessibility statement for the DHT
Explanatory notes: Provide a link to the public accessibility statement
